reason: E2 and E3 show Sn addition promotes BCC phase and increases Hc in FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8Snx, but this is a different base alloy containing Cu and Al, and the hypothesis extrapolates to a simpler FeCoNi system without these elements. The cited evidence does not directly support the claim that a minor Sn addition to equiatomic FeCoNi will produce a dual-phase microstructure with increased coercivity while retaining high Ms and configurational entropy ≥1.0R.
premises: Sn addition to FeCoNi-based alloys promotes formation of a BCC phase alongside FCC
The BCC phase increases coercivity (Hc) in these alloys
The FCC phase maintains high saturation magnetization (Ms) after Sn addition
The dual-phase FCC+BCC microstructure can be achieved at low Sn content (~5-10 at.%) while maintaining high configurational entropy
